planets.name: KELT-16 b
planets.description: Transiting planet of KELT-16 with a 0.969-day year, found in 2017.

text.card: KELT-16 b was found in 2017 by KELT as it crossed its star.
text.introduction: It is the only planet known around KELT-16. Its orbit and size follow Oberst et al. 2017's fit, the archive's default.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table, default parameter set (pl_refname OBERST_ET_AL__2017): disc_year 2017, disc_facility KELT, sy_pnum 1; pl_orbper 0.968992962, pl_radj 1.415, pl_bmassj 2.75

thermal.source: Deming et al. 2023, dayside brightness temperature at 4.5 µm (uniform reanalysis of Spitzer's eclipses, CDS J/AJ/165/104 table 2)
thermal.chosen: 1 measured of 1 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength

phaseCurves.label: Spitzer
phaseCurves.observed: a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 14059)

record.source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of KELT-16b, program 14059, new in this paper. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row KELT-16b, detector model BLISS. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode BLISS_v1 using FWM centroiding), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)).

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
